report.interpretation: Number of auto claims (claim_count, counted by loss date) with loss dates in H1 2025 (Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2025) compared with H1 2026 (Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2026). The result is the percentage change from the first period to the second. Both periods are complete: the extract date is 2026-09-30, and the incomplete-month warning applies only to recent months.
report.answer: Auto claims fell 10.3%, from 1,434 in H1 2025 to 1,287 in H1 2026. This is a raw claim count. I did not adjust for changes in policies in force, so I can't say whether claim frequency fell by the same amount.
report.answer_sql: select sum(case when loss_date between '2025-01-01' and '2025-06-30' then 1 end) h1_2025, sum(case when loss_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-06-30' then 1 end) h1_2026, round(100.0*(sum(case when loss_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-06-30' then 1 end)/sum(case when loss_date between '2025-01-01' and '2025-06-30' then 1 end)-1),1) pct_change from claims where product='auto'

findings.claim: Auto claim count by loss date fell 10.3% from H1 2025 to H1 2026.
findings.evidence_sql: select sum(case when loss_date between '2025-01-01' and '2025-06-30' then 1 end) h1_2025, sum(case when loss_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-06-30' then 1 end) h1_2026, round(100.0*(sum(case when loss_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-06-30' then 1 end)/sum(case when loss_date between '2025-01-01' and '2025-06-30' then 1 end)-1),1) pct_change from claims where product='auto'

data_quality_issues.issue: Claims are reported a median of 4 days after the loss. Late reporting leaves recent months incomplete (September 2026 is about 79% complete).
data_quality_issues.impact: Minimal for this answer. Both half-years ended at least 3 months before the extract date, so only a few very late reports (such as bodily injury) could still be missing, mostly from H1 2026.

open_questions: Do you want claim frequency (claims per 1,000 policies in force) for the same periods? Frequency would show whether the drop reflects fewer policies or fewer claims per policy. I did not run it.
